subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up — Shared vs Dedicated isolation & SLOs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jared Miller <jared.miller@finpay.com>, Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@finpay.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment follow-up — shared vs dedicated isolation & SLOs

Hi Jared / Aisha,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good to hear more about FinPay’s throughput and latency targets for your fraud-detection scoring (real-time scoring on new transactions). Quick recap and next steps below so we’re aligned: 

Recap
- Current traffic shape: ~1.2k TPS at peak for scoring endpoint; 98th percentile request size ~350 tokens.
- Primary concerns: noisy-neighbor interference on shared infra, predictable p99 latency, and compliance around data isolation.
- Desired outcomes: sub-100ms p99 for inference path, predictable monthly unit costs, and clear isolation guarantees for production workloads.

We think there are three deployment modes to evaluate for FinPay: Hosted API (shared), Dedicated (reserved GPU pool), and Private VPC/on-prem. Based on today's discussion, Dedicated capacity looks like the leading candidate but I wanted to confirm a few items: 

Action items / questions for FinPay
1) Is strict single-tenant hardware required, or is logical isolation (dedicated instances + reservations) acceptable?
2) Can you share any SLA or p99 latency targets in writing? You mentioned ~100ms p99 — is that the firm target or a near-term goal?
3) Any regulatory constraints that would force Private VPC/on-prem vs VPC with managed control plane?

Next steps from Redwood
- I’ll loop in Priyom for technical SLO isolation numbers and a draft SLA for Dedicated (attached).
- If you’re open, propose a 2-week POC on a Dedicated pool to validate p99 under your traffic profile. We can run a synthetic replay of your request trace and provide telemetry.

I attached a draft Dedicated SLA and a short infra diagram showing isolation boundaries. Priyom — can you add recommended p99 and tail-latency numbers we can guarantee for Dedicated vs Hosted?

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Deployment follow-up — shared vs dedicated isolation & SLOs

Marissa — thanks for the summary. Quick answers inline:

> 1) Is strict single-tenant hardware required, or is logical isolation acceptable?
Logical isolation is preferred, but if we can demonstrate stable p99 under load we may not need physically single-tenant hardware immediately. Our procurement team will ask for isolation guarantees though.

> 2) Can you share any SLA or p99 latency targets in writing?
We are targeting <= 100ms p99 for the scoring path, ideally with max unrecoverable tail spikes not exceeding 200ms.

> 3) Any regulatory constraints?
We are PCI-adjacent (payments company) — currently not full PCI-SaaS in scope, but our security/compliance team will want evidence of tenant isolation and audit logs. For initial evaluation logical/dedicated is fine.

Also — two additional questions:
- What level of telemetry will we get for noisy neighbor events? (I.e., per-request traces, GPU utilization, and evicted-batch counts)
- If we go Dedicated, how long is typical provisioning lead time for an initial pool?

If you can share the SLA and a short runbook for the POC we’ll route to procurement/security. —Jared

Subject: Re: Deployment follow-up — Shared vs Dedicated isolation & SLOs (SLA + POC runbook attached)

Hi Jared / Aisha,

Quick follow-up — attaching the dedicated SLA draft and a short POC runbook (see attachments). A few clarifications inline to your questions: 

- Telemetry: the POC gives you per-request traces (trace id mapping back to each RPC), per-GPU utilization, queue length, and batched eviction metrics. We also expose KV-cache hit rates and prefix-caching stats.
- Noisy neighbor detection: on Shared (hosted) we provide alerting for sudden p99 regressions and per-tenant percent-of-host resource metrics; on Dedicated we remove noisy-neighbor risk by reserving capacity and offering isolation boundaries — we guarantee no other tenant will be scheduled on the same pool.
- Provisioning lead time: initial Dedicated pool typically 7–10 business days once the order is confirmed; POC can be run faster using a short-lived pre-prod Dedicated pool (3–4 days) if you provide traffic traces.

Suggested SLOs (draft)
- Hosted (shared): best-effort, typical p99 120–250ms depending on load and model; higher variance under bursty traffic.
- Dedicated (reserved pool): targeted p99 <= 100ms under provisioned throughput (we size pool to match replayed trace); max observed uncontended tail rarely exceeds 150–200ms.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): can guarantee isolation and network locality; p99 will depend on your on-prem hardware/ops.

Priyom will add concrete telemetry fields and the runbook steps for the POC (replay, replay metrics, success criteria). If the SLO language looks good I can share the SLA with your procurement team.

Best — Marissa

Hi Jared / Aisha — adding the technical details you asked for and a recommended success criteria for the POC.

Telemetry exposed during POC / Dedicated pool:
- Per-request trace id and timing (ingest -> model token start -> token end -> response)
- Per-GPU utilization (1s, 10s, 1m windows) and per-GPU batch size distribution
- Queue depth and per-route queue latency
- Evicted batch count and batch retry metrics
- KV-cache hit ratio and cache latency

Recommended POC sizing and success criteria:
- Replay your 48-hour peak trace at 1.0x to validate steady-state; if traces are not sharable we can run a synthetic replay with same TPS and token distribution.
- Provision Dedicated pool to handle 1.2k TPS with 20% headroom (we typically recommend 1.2–1.5x for headroom).
- Success = p99 <= 100ms for >= 95% of the replay windows, and no more than 3 isolated tail spikes > 200ms during the run.

Operational notes:
- For procurement: initial Dedicated commitment is monthly; we can provide a 30-day pilot contract for the POC.
- For security: we will provide tenant-level audit logs, access to KMS integration docs, and SOC2 artifacts on request.

Next steps:
1) Marissa: share the SLA doc with procurement.
2) Jared: confirm whether you can provide a traffic trace or prefer synthetic replay.
3) We’ll schedule the POC kickoff once trace/approach confirmed (target start within 3–7 business days after confirmation).

Happy to jump on a short tech call if your infra/security team wants to go deeper.

Thanks — Priyom
